pref.1: Several years of field observations have complicated an earlier explanation of a natural phenomenon, and researchers now describe the situation with more caution than certainty. Their report compares preliminary measurements with older assumptions and emphasizes how much the interpretation depends on incomplete but suggestive evidence gathered across different seasons and locations.
pref.2: A regional archive recently acquired letters, maps, and photographs that changed how historians understand a public project. Because the records were fragmentary, the scholars had to connect small pieces of evidence across several sources before describing the project's development, the people who shaped it, and the reasons its significance had been overlooked.
pref.3: At a community arts center, a curator prepared an exhibition about creators whose work drew on scientific observation, local history, and collaboration. The exhibition notes explain how individual decisions, materials, audiences, and institutional settings shaped the meaning of each work over time rather than treating the finished objects as isolated achievements.
pref.4: A city planning report compares several approaches to improving transportation, public health, and access to shared spaces. The report links individual examples to broader patterns, showing how policy choices can produce effects that are gradual, indirect, or difficult to measure immediately, especially when different neighborhoods experience the same policy in different ways.
pref.5: In a laboratory study, researchers tracked a process over multiple stages and found that the outcome depended on timing, environment, and the interaction of several variables. o29.body: While researching a topic, a student has taken notes about apple varieties. The student wants to explain the decline in the number of commercially grown apple varieties and specify why the decline occurred.
o29.stem: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

opts.A: Many apple varieties have distinctive flavors and textures.
opts.B: Apple growers have cultivated thousands of varieties over time.
opts.C: The number of commercially grown apple varieties declined as growers increasingly favored varieties that shipped well and looked uniform in stores.
opts.D: Some older apple varieties are preserved in specialty orchards.

29.1.body:
Notes: Thousands of fruit varieties were once sold locally; commercial growers later favored fruit that looked uniform and tolerated long shipping; many older varieties became rare.

Goal: explain the decline and specify its cause.
29.1.stem: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

opts.A: Older fruit varieties sometimes have unusual flavors.
opts.B: The number of commercially grown fruit varieties declined because growers increasingly favored uniform varieties that could withstand long-distance shipping.
opts.C: Some local growers preserve rare varieties.
opts.D: Commercial orchards can contain many trees.

29.2.body:
Notes: Several regional rice types were once cultivated; supermarkets preferred grains that cooked consistently and packaged easily; farmers shifted toward those varieties.

Goal: explain the decline and specify its cause.
29.2.stem: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

opts.A: Some regional rice varieties remain in seed banks.
opts.C: Rice can be grown in many climates.
opts.D: Regional rice varieties declined as farmers shifted toward types preferred by supermarkets for consistent cooking and easy packaging.

29.3.body:
Notes: Many local tomato varieties existed; large distributors wanted tomatoes with thick skins and uniform color; growers planted fewer delicate varieties.

Goal: explain the decline and specify its cause.
29.3.stem: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

opts.C: Tomatoes vary in color and flavor.
opts.D: Local tomato varieties became less common because large distributors favored uniform, thick-skinned tomatoes that traveled well.

29.4.body:
Notes: Older wheat varieties were adapted to local soils; industrial mills preferred wheat with predictable protein levels; farmers increasingly planted mill-preferred varieties.

Goal: explain the decline and specify its cause.
29.4.stem: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

opts.A: Older wheat varieties declined as farmers adopted varieties with predictable protein levels preferred by industrial mills.
opts.B: Local soils can affect crop yields.
opts.C: Wheat has been cultivated for thousands of years.

29.5.body:
Notes: Many bean varieties were once grown in mountain villages; export buyers wanted beans of a single size and color; farmers reduced the number of varieties they planted.

Goal: explain the decline and specify its cause.
29.5.stem: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

opts.A: Some buyers purchase crops for export.
opts.B: Beans are a source of protein.
opts.C: The number of bean varieties planted in mountain villages declined because export buyers preferred beans of a single size and color.
opts.D: Mountain villages often have small farms.

o33.stem: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

opts.A: Rogers and Russell investigated whether woodland expansion was related to climate patterns.
opts.B: Woodland expansion can affect grassland ecosystems.
opts.C: Climate patterns vary by region and over time.
opts.D: Rogers and Russell compared several environmental factors.

opts.A: Rainfall records are one kind of climate data.
opts.C: The researchers investigated whether woodland expansion was associated with changes in rainfall patterns.
opts.D: Tree-cover maps can show where forests grow.

33.2.body:
Notes: A team measured lake levels and temperature records; they wanted to test whether warming was linked to changes in evaporation.

Goal: state the aim of a study.

opts.A: Temperature records are useful to scientists.
opts.B: The team sought to determine whether rising temperatures were linked to changes in lake evaporation.
